display.purpose: The single page headline, two lines at most, max 16ch.

title.purpose: Sub-blocks, exit-row titles; the wordmark at 800.

code.purpose: Commands, paths and real output only; ligatures off.

exit-digit.purpose: The digit inside an exit-code keycap.

shadows.name: raised
shadows.value: 8px 8px 18px var(--lo), -8px -8px 18px var(--hi), inset 0 0 0 var(--lo), inset 0 0 0 var(--hi)
shadows.purpose: The install slab, the walk band, surfaced findings.

shadows.name: raised-sm
shadows.value: 5px 5px 11px var(--lo), -5px -5px 11px var(--hi), inset 0 0 0 var(--lo), inset 0 0 0 var(--hi)

shadows.name: pressed
shadows.value: 0 0 0 var(--lo), 0 0 0 var(--hi), inset 5px 5px 10px var(--lo), inset -5px -5px 10px var(--hi)
shadows.purpose: Wells, used files, chips, the CI block, exit rows, the switch track, pressed buttons.

shadows.name: pressed-deep
shadows.value: 0 0 0 var(--lo), 0 0 0 var(--hi), inset 10px 10px 22px var(--lo), inset -10px -10px 22px var(--hi)

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: Every state change: press, rise, fade, theme switch.

motion.name: rise
motion.purpose: A finding rising out of the ground: 500ms initial delay, 420ms stagger in report order.

motion.name: confidence-reveal
motion.purpose: The high label fading in behind its risen tile.

motion.name: verdict
motion.purpose: Summary and exit keycap appearing 700ms after the last finding.

motion.name: theme
motion.purpose: Ground and ink crossfade on theme switch.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: All transition durations and delays zeroed; the scan shows its final state at once.

narrative.overview:
The whole interface is one continuous soft material, pressed and raised like a single cast surface. Nothing sits on top of the page; everything is formed out of it. Ordinary content is pressed into the ground, and the things that matter, the findings and the actions, rise out of it. This matches what exhume does: it digs a workspace and lifts out the files nothing imports.

The material is neumorphic, but it serves a working tool, not an app-store showcase. Type is tight and heavy, paths and output are set in real monospace, and depth carries meaning rather than decoration. The surface exists in two full renditions, a cool daylight clay and a deep night clay. Neither is a filtered copy of the other.

Density is generous around headings and tight inside groups. One accent colour does all the signalling, and every line of output shown is real.
keyCharacteristics: One material per theme; surfaces are pressed or raised, never layered or floating.
Raised means "this matters": findings, primary actions, keycaps.
Pressed means "this is context": wells, used files, chips, code.
A single accent, Verdigris, marks confidence labels, the primary action and focus.
Light and dark are both first-class and follow the OS, with a remembered manual switch.

rules.name: The One Patina Rule
rules.body: Verdigris is the only colour that is not clay or ink. It marks findings, the primary action and focus, and nothing decorative.

rules.name: The Same Clay Rule
rules.body: A control never gets its own fill. It is the ground colour, shaped by light. A filled button is a sticker on the material.

rules.name: The Real Mono Rule
rules.body: Monospace is for things a terminal would print: commands, paths, output. Never for decoration, eyebrows or labels. Workspace names in prose, such as the supported-setup chips, stay in the grotesk.

rules.name: The No Eyebrow Rule
rules.body: Headings carry their own weight. No kicker or small label above them.

rules.name: The Typed As Shown Rule
rules.body: Code renders exactly what a visitor would type: ligatures are disabled (`--` and `>-` stay two glyphs), and mono paths and commands break only at a space or right after a single `/`. `file.ts:1:1` stays whole, `pnpm-monorepo` never splits at its hyphen, and `https://` stays attached to its host.

rules.name: The Rise Means Found Rule
rules.body: Only a finding or an action may be raised inside a pressed area. If it's raised, it must matter.

rules.name: The Never Shadow Alone Rule
rules.body: Raised versus pressed is never the only signal. A raised finding also changes ink weight and gains its `high` label, so the state survives low-contrast screens and colour-blind viewers.

dos: **Do** build every surface from the ground colour and shape it with the four-shadow vocabulary.
**Do** keep body, path and button text at 4.5:1 or better against the ground, in both themes.
**Do** render every state (copy default, pressed, copied, selected, the scan sequence, the reduced-motion and no-JavaScript fallbacks) in both themes.
**Do** show real exhume output, unedited, wherever output appears.
**Do** theme the browser surfaces: selection in Verdigris Select, scrollbars in Shadow on the ground, focus rings in Verdigris, the browser theme colour in the ground.
**Do** let column-aligned output scroll inside its well on narrow screens, with the right-edge fade, rather than rewrap it.
donts: **Don't** dim or partially fade an element to show a state; neumorphism already runs low contrast. Opacity only takes an element from absent to present during the scan sequence.
**Don't** give a button or panel its own fill colour, gradient, glow or glass.
**Don't** nest a raised card inside a raised card, or float anything above the ground.
**Don't** use monospace for anything that isn't a command, path or output.
**Don't** let a mono path or command break mid-token or render a ligature.
**Don't** set a sentence-long headline at display size beyond two lines.
**Don't** let a soft, toy-like or app-store look creep in: no bouncy easing, pastel accents or rounded-blob illustrations.
